title: Pillars of Creation (original 1995 WFPC2)
wavelengths: F502N [O III] 502 nm = blue; F656N H-alpha 656 nm = green; F673N [S II] 673 nm = red
credit_line: Jeff Hester and Paul Scowen (Arizona State University), and NASA/ESA
notes: The iconic image (released 2 Nov 1995, Hester et al. 1996 AJ 111, 2349). Staircase-shaped WFPC2 mosaic with the black missing corner (PC chip). EGGs visible as tiny fingertips on pillar tops.

title: Evaporating gaseous globules (EGGs) in M16
wavelengths: same as opo9544a
credit_line: Jeff Hester and Paul Scowen (Arizona State University), and NASA/ESA
notes: Close-up of the top of the tallest pillar showing finger-like EGGs being uncovered by photoevaporation.

title: New view of the Pillars of Creation - visible
wavelengths: [O III] 502 nm (F502N) = blue; H-alpha+[N II] 657 nm (F657N) = green; [S II] 673 nm (F673N) = orange/red
credit_line: NASA, ESA/Hubble and the Hubble Heritage Team
notes: Released 5 Jan 2015 (AAS 225), observed Sep 2014 for Hubble's 25th anniversary (proposal 13926, Z. Levay). Downscaled to 2400 px from 6 MB publication JPEG.

title: New view of the Pillars of Creation - infrared
wavelengths: F110W ~1.1 um and F160W ~1.6 um (near-IR)
credit_line: NASA, ESA/Hubble and the Hubble Heritage Team
notes: Dust becomes translucent; pillars are ghostly silhouettes, embedded and background stars appear. Downscaled to 2400 px.

title: The Pillars of Creation - 1995 and 2015 comparison
wavelengths: narrowband [O III], H-alpha, [S II]
credit_line: WFC3: NASA, ESA/Hubble and the Hubble Heritage Team WFPC2: NASA, ESA/Hubble, STScI, J. Hester and P. Scowen (Arizona State University)
notes: Side-by-side over a 20-year baseline: shows small changes in the pillar edges and a jet-like feature at the top of the left pillar (see ESA caption for measured motions).

title: Digitized Sky Survey image of the Eagle Nebula
wavelengths: DSS2 blue + red plates
credit_line: ESO/Digitized Sky Survey 2. Acknowledgment: Davide De Martin.
notes: Ground-based context view of the whole nebula; use for zoom-in starting frame.

title: Webb's Pillars of Creation (NIRCam, cropped)
wavelengths: F090W 0.9 um = purple; F187N Pa-alpha 1.87 um = blue; F200W 2.0 um = cyan; F335M PAH 3.35 um = yellow; F444W 4.44 um = orange; F470N H2 4.7 um = red
credit_line: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; J. DePasquale, A. Koekemoer, A. Pagan (STScI).
notes: Released 19 Oct 2022. Same framing as Hubble 2014. Red wavy lines/lava-like edges at pillar tips = H2 shocks from young-star outflows/jets. Downscaled to 2400 px.

title: Pillars of Creation (MIRI image)
wavelengths: F770W 7.7 um = blue; F1130W 11.3 um = green; F1500W 15 um = red
credit_line: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, J. DePasquale (STScI), A. Pagan (STScI)
notes: Released 28 Oct 2022. Dust glow dominates; most stars vanish; grey-blue dust and ashen pillars, red tinges = densest/coolest dust where stars are still forming.

title: Pillars of Creation (NIRCam and MIRI composite)
wavelengths: Purple F090W; Blue F187N + F770W; Cyan F200W; Green F1130W; Yellow F335M; Orange F444W; Red F470N + F1500W

credit_line: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI; Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI), Alyssa Pagan (STScI), Anton Koekemoer (STScI)
notes: Released 30 Nov 2022. Downloaded the 2000x1872 PNG rendition and converted to JPEG q85 (full res is 7130x6675, 58 MB). Data: JWST program 2739 (PI K. Pontoppidan), observed 14 Aug 2022.

title: Hubble and Webb showcase the Pillars of Creation (side by side)

credit_line: ESO
notes: Whole nebula: Pillars at centre, NGC 6611 cluster upper right, 'The Spire' (Fairy) middle left. Downscaled to 2400 px.

title: The Eagle's EGGs (VLT ISAAC near-infrared)
wavelengths: J 1.24 um = blue; H 1.65 um = green; Ks 2.16 um = red
credit_line: ESO/M.McCaughrean & M.Andersen (AIP)
notes: 9x9 arcmin near-IR view (McCaughrean & Andersen 2002); showed most EGGs are empty, only ~15% host young stars; a massive young star in the head of column 1. Downscaled to 2000 px.

title: Colour composite of the Pillars of Creation from MUSE data

credit_line: ESO
notes: McLeod et al. 2015 (MNRAS 450, 1057): 3D orientation of the pillars, photoevaporation mass-loss rate (~70 Msun/Myr) -> pillars survive ~3 Myr. Also new jet detected in the middle pillar.

title: The Eagle Nebula (M16) - Chandra X-ray + Hubble optical

title: The Eagle Nebula (M16): Peering into the Pillars of Creation

notes: Not downloaded (576 px). Linsky et al. 2007: few X-ray sources in pillars -> star formation there may be past its peak.

title: Cosmic Epic Unfolds in Infrared (Spitzer)
wavelengths: 4.5 um = blue; 8 um = green; 24 um = red
license: Public domain (NASA media guidelines; credit requested)
credit_line: NASA/JPL-Caltech/STScI/ Institut d'Astrophysique Spatiale
notes: PIA09107, Jan 2007 (Flagey et al.). Green = cooler dust incl. pillars; red shell of hot dust interpreted as heated by a supernova ~8,000-9,000 yr ago; shock wave estimated to have toppled the pillars ~6,000 yr ago, light of which would reach us in ~1,000 yr. Interpretation, contested (dust could be heated by stellar winds).
